Container.Name: SD-WebUI-Forge-Neo-Unraid
Container.Description:
Forge Neo (Stable Diffusion WebUI) by Haoming02, packaged for Unraid by Aegisnir, with security hardening. Forge Neo is Haoming02's work: https://github.com/Haoming02/sd-webui-forge-classic/tree/neo This container only packages it for Unraid. Please report WebUI bugs upstream.
Image: ghcr.io/aegisnir/sd-webui-forge-neo-unraid:dev
README: https://github.com/aegisnir/sd-webui-forge-neo-unraid/blob/dev/README.md
## Extra Parameters (advanced view), flag by flag - --runtime=nvidia: gives the container your NVIDIA GPU. Don't remove it; GPU choice is the GPU (NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES) setting. - --read-only: the container's own files can't be changed; only /data, /config and /tmp are writable. - --tmpfs /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,nodev,size=2g: a 2 GB scratch area in RAM; nothing can be run from it; cleared on restart. - --security-opt no-new-privileges:true: processes can never gain more rights than they started with. - --cap-drop=ALL: removes root's special powers inside the container. - --cap-add=CHOWN, FOWNER: gives back only what startup needs to fix /data and /config ownership. - --cap-add=SETUID, SETGID: lets startup switch from root to the WebUI user (99:100). Removing them stops the container from starting. - --pids-limit=2048: at most 2048 processes, so a runaway extension can't freeze Unraid. Full explanation, with what happens if you remove each one: README, Security Hardening Defaults.
DATA DIRECTORY WARNING: The path used with --data-dir grows very large very quickly because it can hold models, outputs, extensions, caches, and other working data. I recommend storing it outside of appdata when possible. You can still place it inside appdata if you want the convenience, but it may consume space very quickly and can fill the location you use for Docker-related storage.
The default host path is set to /mnt/user/ai/data/ so the large working set lives outside appdata by default.
Self-healing data directory: The container automatically corrects /data ownership on startup if it is owned by another user (for example, after deleting the host data path, or data copied from another container). Folders mapped in separately (the optional Models and Outputs directories) are never re-owned; the log warns if they aren't writable. In most cases no user action is needed. A log message will confirm when ownership was corrected. If the auto-fix fails (NFS root squash, unusual host permissions), the log will explain the manual fix.
Authentication defaults: This container uses auth-file based login by default. On first launch, startup seeds /config/auth/webui-auth.txt if missing. Default end-user login (first launch): admin / changeme Startup does not block this default; change it after first login for normal use. Use WEBUI_AUTH_FILE to override the auth-file path if needed. Recommended auth file path: /config/auth/webui-auth.txt Example syntax: - one per line: admin:strong-password - or comma-separated: admin:strong-password,viewer:another-password - lines starting with # are ignored as comments
Model checkpoint note: Forge Neo never downloads a model on its own. Add a .safetensors file under /data/models/Stable-diffusion.
Log safety: Sensitive auth flags (--gradio-auth, --gradio-auth-path, --api-auth) have their values replaced with <redacted> in startup log output, so logs are safe to share.
Built-in healthcheck: The image includes a Docker HEALTHCHECK that probes port 7860. It uses generous timers (5 min start grace, 5 retries) to avoid false positives during model loading or heavy extension operations. Unhealthy status is informational only and does not auto-restart the container.
Container.Overview:
Image: ghcr.io/aegisnir/sd-webui-forge-neo-unraid:dev Extra Parameters (advanced view) hold --runtime=nvidia (the GPU) and the security options; each is explained in the Description and the README. Full setup and usage docs: https://github.com/aegisnir/sd-webui-forge-neo-unraid/blob/dev/README.md
This template passes Forge Neo data storage through --data-dir.
- Models, outputs, extensions, caches, and other working data are stored in the mapped data share instead of the container filesystem. - Python, PyTorch and all WebUI dependencies are built into the image, so startup needs no downloads (extensions may still install their own packages). - The data directory can grow very large very quickly, so I recommend storing it outside of appdata when possible. - Launch flags are options in this template (common ones visible, the rest under Show more settings). Anything else goes in Extra Launch Flags. - If startup fails with a Torch GPU check error, you can temporarily add --skip-torch-cuda-test to Extra Launch Flags for troubleshooting. - If an extension breaks torch, delete /data/python-user on the host and restart. It holds only packages installed by extensions. - WebUI login is enabled by default unless you explicitly set your own --gradio-auth or --gradio-auth-path in Extra Launch Flags. - Container logs annotate known harmless warnings inline and display a [READY] box when the WebUI is accepting connections. - A built-in Docker healthcheck monitors port 7860 with conservative timers to avoid false positives during heavy operations.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Port on your server for the WebUI (default 7860). The WebUI always uses 7860 inside the container; change this to use a different port on your server.

Config.Name: Config Directory
Config.Description: Host path for auth files and WebUI settings (appdata). Kept separate from the large AI data share so it can be backed up with standard Unraid appdata backup tools. Default: /mnt/user/appdata/SD-WebUI-Forge-Neo-Unraid

Config.Name: Data Directory
Config.Description: Host path for everything the WebUI stores: models, outputs, extensions and caches. This one folder handles everything. Default: /mnt/user/ai/data/ (outside appdata).

Config.Name: Models Directory (optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Leave empty: models stay inside the Data Directory, which handles everything. Fill in only for more granular control, for example a separate models share you also use elsewhere. Move your existing models first: this hides the Data Directory's own models folder. The container never changes this folder's owner; it must be writable by 99:100 (nobody:users).

Config.Name: Outputs Directory (optional)
Config.Description: OPTIONAL. Leave empty: images are saved inside the Data Directory, which handles everything. Fill in only for more granular control, for example a share you browse from another computer. The container never changes this folder's owner; it must be writable by 99:100 (nobody:users).

Config.Name: WebUI Auth File
Config.Description: Path inside the container to the WebUI auth file (recommended/default: /config/auth/webui-auth.txt). If the file is missing on first launch, startup seeds it from the repository default template. Default seeded login is admin:changeme. Format: username:password per line, or comma-separated entries on one line. Blank lines and # comments are ignored. For security, change the default password after first login.

Config.Name: HTTPS
Config.Description: auto (default): serve HTTPS. Uses /config/tls/custom.crt and custom.key if you provide both, otherwise a self-signed certificate created in /config/tls (your browser warns once; compare the SHA-256 fingerprint printed in the log). off: plain HTTP.

Config.Name: HTTPS Hostnames
Config.Description: Recommended: the full hostname (FQDN) you open the WebUI with, then the server's IP, separated by a comma with no spaces. Example: myserver.example.com,192.168.1.10. Both are added to the self-signed certificate so the browser's address matches it either way.

Config.Name: GPU (NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES)
Config.Description: Which NVIDIA GPUs this container gets. all (default), or one GPU's UUID (shown by the Unraid NVIDIA driver plugin, or nvidia-smi -L), to keep other GPUs for Plex or a VM. Works together with --runtime=nvidia in Extra Parameters.

Config.Name: Install extensions from the WebUI
Config.Description: MAINTAINER'S CHOICE: true (Forge Neo's default is false). Lets anyone who can log in install extensions, and extensions run their own code inside the container. false locks the Extensions tab to what is installed. (--enable-insecure-extension-access)

Config.Name: API
Config.Description: Turns on Forge Neo's REST API (--api). Needed by every other API option and by API Auth File Mode. Off by default.

Config.Name: API only (no WebUI)
Config.Description: Starts only the API, without the browser UI (--nowebui). Turns the API on by itself.

Config.Name: CUDA malloc
Config.Description: MAINTAINER'S CHOICE: true (Forge Neo's default is false). Faster GPU memory allocation (--cuda-malloc). Forge Neo's own log recommends it on RTX cards, and Neo skips it on cards that can't use it. WARNING: if you see CUDA memory errors or crashes, set this to false first. ALSO: the Torch Compile presets max-autotune and reduce-overhead do not work while this is on; set it to false to use them.

Config.Name: CUDA streams
Config.Description: Faster offloading of model weights between RAM and VRAM (--cuda-stream N). Off by default.

Config.Name: Pin shared memory
Config.Description: Better RAM use when models are offloaded (--pin-shared-memory). Off by default.

Config.Name: VRAM mode
Config.Description: normal (default) lets Forge Neo decide. lowvram: GPUs with little memory (slower). novram: when even lowvram isn't enough. highvram: keep models in VRAM. gpu-only: everything on the GPU.

Config.Name: Attention package
Config.Description: none (default) uses PyTorch's built-in attention, which Forge Neo calls usually as fast and more stable. Another choice downloads and installs that package at startup into /data/python-user; it is not part of the scanned image. xformers does not support RTX 50 cards.

Config.Name: Theme
Config.Description: WebUI color theme (--theme). default follows your browser.

Config.Name: Extra Launch Flags
Config.Description: Any other Forge Neo flag, separated by spaces. Empty by default. The options above always win: a flag here that an option controls is removed with a log message, as are --listen, --port, --data-dir (the container sets these) and --share/--ngrok (public tunnels). Old A1111/Forge flags that Forge Neo dropped (--xformers-flash-attention, --opt-sdp-attention, --medvram, --no-half-vae and more) are removed with a note on what replaced them: you don't need them here. Forge Neo stops on other flags it doesn't know. List of flags: see the README, Launch options and Migration Notes.

Config.Name: API request logging
Config.Description: NEEDS API = true; ignored otherwise. Logs every API request (--api-log).

Config.Name: API server stop/restart
Config.Description: NEEDS API = true; ignored otherwise. Lets API clients stop or restart the server (--api-server-stop).

Config.Name: API Auth File Mode
Config.Description: NEEDS API = true; does nothing otherwise. mirror-webui-file uses the WebUI login file for the API too (--api-auth). disabled (default) leaves the API without a login unless you pass your own --api-auth in Extra Launch Flags.

Config.Name: Expandable segments
Config.Description: Experimental PyTorch memory allocator; may prevent out-of-memory errors (--expandable-segments).

Config.Name: Fast fp8
Config.Description: Faster math for float8_e4m3fn models (--fast-fp8).

Config.Name: Fast fp16
Config.Description: fp16 accumulation (--fast-fp16).

Config.Name: Autotune
Config.Description: cuDNN benchmark (--autotune). Forge Neo's author: slower in my experience.

Config.Name: Comfy-Kitchen attention
Config.Description: Use Comfy-Kitchen attention; overrides other attention packages (--use-ck-attention).

Config.Name: Triton backend
Config.Description: Triton backend for Comfy-Kitchen; might speed things up (--enable-triton-backend).

Config.Name: pyNVML VRAM tracking
Config.Description: More accurate free-VRAM readings (--pynvml). Installs a package at startup into /data/python-user.

Config.Name: Nunchaku
Config.Description: For SVDQ models (--nunchaku). Installs a package at startup into /data/python-user.

Config.Name: Tiled Conv2d
Config.Description: 0 (default) is off. 64-512: less VRAM for the VAE, slower (--tiled-conv2d).

Config.Name: Reserve VRAM (GB)
Config.Description: VRAM to leave free for other programs, in GB, for example 2 (--reserve-vram). Empty: Forge Neo decides.

Config.Name: Disable smart memory
Config.Description: Offload models to RAM aggressively instead of keeping them in VRAM (--disable-smart-memory).

Config.Name: Force non-blocking
Config.Description: Non-blocking operations for all applicable tensors (--force-non-blocking).

Config.Name: Precision
Config.Description: Force fp32 or fp16 everywhere (--force-fp32 / --force-fp16). auto (default) lets Forge Neo decide.

Config.Name: Diffusion model precision
Config.Description: How the diffusion model is stored (--fp32-unet, --bf16-unet, ...). auto (default) lets Forge Neo decide.

Config.Name: VAE precision
Config.Description: How the VAE is stored. fp16 may cause black images. auto (default) lets Forge Neo decide.

Config.Name: Text encoder precision
Config.Description: How the text encoder is stored. auto (default) lets Forge Neo decide.

Config.Name: VAE on CPU
Config.Description: Run the VAE on the CPU: saves VRAM, much slower (--cpu-vae).

Config.Name: Text encoder on CPU
Config.Description: Run the text encoder on the CPU: saves VRAM, slower (--cpu-text-enc).

Config.Name: Disable sage
Config.Description: Skip an installed sageattention package (--disable-sage).

Config.Name: Disable flash
Config.Description: Skip an installed flash_attn package (--disable-flash).

Config.Name: Disable xformers
Config.Description: Skip an installed xformers package (--disable-xformers).

Config.Name: Models folder override
Config.Description: NEEDS A PATH MAPPING FIRST. A container path, for example /models, that replaces the models folder (--model-ref). The optional Models Directory path above is usually simpler.

Config.Name: ComfyUI models
Config.Description: NEEDS A PATH MAPPING FIRST. Map your ComfyUI folder (for example to /comfyui) with Add another Path, then enter that container path here to also load ComfyUI's models (--forge-ref-comfy-home).

Config.Name: A1111 models
Config.Description: NEEDS A PATH MAPPING FIRST. Same idea for an AUTOMATIC1111 install (--forge-ref-a1111-home).

Config.Name: Lock settings
Config.Description: Nobody can change settings in the WebUI (--freeze-settings).

Config.Name: Hide folder settings
Config.Description: Hide output-folder settings in the WebUI (--hide-ui-dir-config).

Config.Name: Extensions
Config.Description: enabled (default). builtin-only or disabled, to troubleshoot a broken extension (--disable-extra-extensions / --disable-all-extensions).

Config.Name: Update extensions on start
Config.Description: MAINTAINER'S CHOICE: true (Forge Neo's default is false). Pulls updates for every installed extension on each start (--update-all-extensions). Trade-off: new extension code runs without you reviewing it, and an update can break an extension. false: update by hand from the Extensions tab.

Config.Name: Reverse-proxy subpath
Config.Description: For a reverse proxy that serves the WebUI under a path, for example sd (--subpath). Empty by default.

Config.Name: No checkpoint hashing
Config.Description: Faster model loading; model hashes are missing from image info (--no-hashing).

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: Forge Neo's log detail (--loglevel).

Config.Name: GPU driver capabilities
Config.Description: Which NVIDIA driver features the container gets. compute runs PyTorch; utility gives nvidia-smi. Leave as is.

Config.Name: Login Attempts
Config.Description: Failed logins for one username before it is locked. 0 turns login protection off. Locked out? Restart the container.

Config.Name: Login Lockout Minutes
Config.Description: How long a username stays locked after too many failed logins.

Config.Name: Server IP for the log
Config.Description: Optional. Your Unraid server's IP, shown in the [READY] log box and added to the self-signed certificate. Does not change where the WebUI listens.

Config.Name: Restart WebUI on exit
Config.Description: 1 (default): restart the WebUI after it exits or crashes (needed for the Restart button). 0: stop the container instead.

Config.Name: Restart delay (s)
Config.Description: Seconds to wait before restarting after a clean exit.

Config.Name: Crash restart delay max (s)
Config.Description: Longest wait between restarts after repeated crashes.

Config.Name: Crash restart attempts
Config.Description: 0 (default): keep retrying. N: stop after N crashes in a row.

Config.Name: App User ID
Config.Description: User ID the WebUI runs as. Default 99 (Unraid's nobody) fits most setups. On first start, /data and /config are re-owned to this user (separately mapped folders, such as the optional Models and Outputs directories, never are). Must be a number other than 0.

Config.Name: App Group ID
Config.Description: Group ID the WebUI runs as. Default 100 (Unraid's users). Must be a number other than 0.

Config.Name: UMASK
Config.Description: Optional file creation mask (octal), for example 0027. Leave empty to keep the container default behavior and easier host-side access.
